title: Preparing for Independence
subtitle: A date was set, and then the world got in the way.
objectives: Explain what the Tydings-McDuffie Act set in motion
Describe the Commonwealth and its purpose
Name the leaders of the transition

cards.title: Independence was scheduled, not sudden
cards.text: Term 1 ended with American colonial government. This term opens with the Americans agreeing to leave. On a timetable.

cards.title: The Tydings-McDuffie Act, 1934
cards.text: The United States Congress passed a law setting a date for Philippine independence.
points: **Ten years of transition**, then full independence.
**A Commonwealth** would govern in the meantime.
**Foreign policy stayed American** during those ten years.
**The date set was 1945.** It did not happen then.

cards.title: A government with real power and real limits
cards.text: Established 1935. Filipinos ran most things; the United States kept some control.
points: **Manuel L. Quezon** was elected President.
**Sergio Osmeña** was Vice President.
**Its own constitution**, written in 1935.
**Defence and foreign affairs** remained American.

cards.title: A ten-year countdown
cards.text: Tap each stop. The last one is where the clock stops.

question.text: What did the Tydings-McDuffie Act establish?
question.explain: A scheduled ten-year Commonwealth period, then independence.

cards.title: Quezon's line about running a government
cards.text: He said he would rather have a country run like hell by Filipinos than like heaven by Americans.
points: **It is quoted constantly**, and it is about self-rule.
**Better imperfect and ours** than perfect and someone else's.
**He also built institutions** that outlived him.
**He died in 1944**, before independence came.

cards.title: What a country does before it governs itself
cards.text: The Commonwealth years were spent building the machinery of a state.
points: **A national language** was chosen, based on Tagalog.
**A national defence act** created an army.
**Public education** expanded.
**Land reform was tried**, with limited success.

question.text: The Commonwealth had complete control over foreign policy.
question.explain: Defence and foreign affairs stayed with the United States throughout the transition.

cards.title: Why 1945 came and went
cards.text: The schedule was interrupted by something nobody in 1934 had planned for.
points: **Japan invaded in December 1941.**
**The Commonwealth government fled** into exile.
**Three years of occupation** followed.
**Independence finally came on 4 July 1946.**

cards.title: The war reached Luzon within hours
cards.text: Clark Field was attacked on 8 December 1941, the same day as Pearl Harbor across the date line.
points: **Most of the air force** was destroyed on the ground.
**Warning had been received** and the aircraft were still parked.
**Without air cover** the defence of Luzon was decided early.
**The ten-year plan** ended that morning.

options: The Japanese occupation and the war
question.explain: The invasion and occupation interrupted the timetable entirely.

cards.title: A country being assembled
cards.alt: A Philippine flag flying open against a blue sky, its sun and three stars visible
cards.text: A flag, an army, a language, a president. All of it built inside ten years.

terms.def: The 1934 US law setting a ten-year path to Philippine independence.
Vice President, later President after Quezon's death.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Tydings-McDuffie, 1934: ten years, then independence.
The Commonwealth began in 1935 under Quezon.
Defence and foreign policy stayed American.
War delayed independence from 1945 to 4 July 1946.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 1 Social Studies, picking up exactly where Term 1 left off with American colonial government. The organising idea is that independence was scheduled rather than won suddenly, which makes the Commonwealth years intelligible as preparation rather than as a pause. The limits on the Commonwealth (defence and foreign affairs staying American) are given directly, because 'self-governing' without those qualifications is the version most learners carry away. The week ends on the gap between the planned 1945 date and the actual 1946 one, which sets up the occupation in weeks 3 and 4.
discussion: Why would a colonial power schedule its own departure?
What does Quezon's famous line actually argue for?
What has to exist before a country can govern itself?
extension: List the institutions a new country needs on day one.
Find out what your own province was like in the 1930s.
misconceptions: That the Commonwealth was fully independent.
That independence happened in 1945 as planned.
That Quezon lived to see it.
